question.text: AIF Category II includes which of the following fund types?

answer.text: Venture Capital Funds and Social Venture Funds
Private Equity Funds and Debt Funds

explanation.text: The Logic: AIF Category II is the residual AIF category for funds that do not fall under Category I or Category III. Workbook-supported Category II fund types include Private Equity Funds and Debt Funds. Category II AIFs are close-ended with a minimum tenure of three years and do not undertake leverage or borrowing other than to meet day-to-day operational requirements. The Trap: Venture Capital Funds and Social Venture Funds (option A) sit in Category I. Hedge Funds and PIPE Funds (option B) sound sophisticated like Category II vehicles, but they sit in Category III because of complex/leveraged strategies. Infrastructure Funds and SME Funds (option D) are Category I sub-types. Note: The cited workbook chapter (NISM-Series-X-A Investment Adviser (Level 1) - June 2025.pdf, p. 237) supports Private Equity Funds and Debt Funds as Category II but does not specifically classify Fund of Funds as a Category II type, so the option text has been narrowed accordingly. The framing above is general industry/regulatory knowledge of SEBI's AIF category structure.
